data.title: Bill Ackman Warns Fed May Have Made A ‘Mistake’, Says AI Could Break Its Inflation Model
data.description:
Key points:
  • Ackman argued that demand for AI-fueled demand for infrastructure and energy may behave differently from the demand typically affected by higher borrowing costs.
  • He added that the potential payoff from developing “super intelligence” could keep AI infrastructure spending high even as interest rates rise.
  • Ackman said this could weaken a key monetary-policy channel, which is that higher borrowing costs typically curb investment and demand.

Billionaire hedge fund manager Bill Ackman questioned whether the Federal Reserve’s traditional approach to fighting inflation still works in an economy increasingly shaped by AI, energy demand and massive investment in computing infrastructure.

In a post on X, the Pershing Square Capital Management founder argued that the current AI boom could create an unusual economic environment in which higher interest rates do not necessarily reduce demand or investment as expected.

AI Could Challenge The Fed’s Inflation Playbook, Says Ackman

Ackman argued that demand for AI-fueled demand for infrastructure and energy may behave differently from the demand typically affected by higher borrowing costs.

He pointed to the potentially enormous economic payoff from winning the race to develop “super intelligence,” arguing that the return on investment could be so large that companies and governments may continue spending heavily on AI infrastructure even as interest rates rise.

Ackman added that this could weaken one of the key channels through which monetary policy is supposed to work, which is that higher rates make borrowing more expensive, which typically discourages investment and demand.

But if demand for computing power, energy and AI infrastructure remains exceptionally strong regardless of financing costs, Ackman questions whether rate hikes would have the same disinflationary effect they have had in previous economic cycles.

Earlier this month, the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) data showed that the Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 0.4% in August on a seasonally adjusted basis, with the annual inflation rate remaining unchanged at 3.4%.

Core CPI, which excludes food and energy, rose 0.3% in August, with the annual inflation rate cooling to 2.4% from 2.5% in July.

Could Higher Rates Actually Add To Inflation?

Ackman also raised concerns about another possibility, which is that higher rates could themselves become an additional source of inflation if elevated financing costs are increasingly embedded into the prices of goods and services.

“Why won’t higher rates at this unique moment in history therefore lead to more inflation as interest costs are embedded in everything?” he asked.

The billionaire investor expressed concerns that this could kickstart a vicious cycle, wherein higher rates increase costs across the economy without sufficiently reducing demand, resulting in inflation remaining elevated. The Fed could then respond with even higher rates, potentially pushing costs up further, he argued.

“What if the old models don’t apply to the current paradigm and the Fed is wrong?” Ackman asked. He concluded that the Fed “might have just made a mistake.”

Ackman’s concerns come after the Federal Open Market Committee raised the benchmark interest rate target by 25 basis points to 3.75% to 4%. Addressing reporters following the decision, Fed Chair Kevin Warsh noted that AI-related equipment and software investment has surged nearly 20% over the past year, supporting manufacturing and future growth. However, he said the timing and scale of its impact on the economy’s supply side remain uncertain.

During the after-hours session on Friday, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), which tracks the S&P 500 index, rose 0.09%; the Invesco QQQ Trust ETF (QQQ) gained 0.12%; and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) rose 0.04%. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits toward the S&P 500 ETF was in the ‘extremely bullish’ territory at the time of writing.

data.title: On Michigan doorsteps, Republicans sell Democrats-as-extremists message with mixed success
data.description:
Key points:
  • Michigan Senate race key test of whether Republican ground game can overcome enthusiasm gap
  • Republicans betting Trump's star power can boost turnout among infrequent voters
  • Rogers mounting expansive turnout effort, backed by outside groups

By Nathan Layne

The pitch was simple: Republican US Senate candidate Mike Rogers is a common-sense conservative, while Democratic rival Abdul El-Sayed is a big-government socialist aligned with the party's left wing.

But when a canvasser backing Rogers delivered that message to Nick Delise, a three-time Donald Trump voter in suburban Detroit, he encountered some skepticism. Though Delise said he would probably vote for Rogers, he rejected the notion that Democrats were controlled by the far left, saying the party was focused on practical solutions to voters' problems.

The exchange offered a first-hand look at a strategy Republicans are deploying in Michigan and other battleground states: to portray Democrats as ideological extremists who have moved too far to the left, while turning out less-engaged supporters needed to keep their congressional majorities in November.

Reuters accompanied door-knockers with Americans for Prosperity Action, the super PAC arm of the conservative network backed by billionaire Charles Koch, in the city of Livonia last week as they sought to mobilize voters for Rogers in the tightly contested race.

The conversations highlighted both the appeal and limits of Republican messaging. With many Americans unhappy with President Donald Trump's handling of the economy and the war in Iran, Republicans have been struggling to find messages that will get voters grappling with the high cost of living to the polls on Election Day.

Delise, 32, had appeared an ideal audience for the pitch. An American flag hung from the porch of his modest, single-story home, two pickup trucks sat in the driveway and a pro-police "Thin Blue Line" banner was displayed in the garage.

He acknowledged he knew little about the candidates and typically skips midterm elections, while attributing his conservative leanings to the influence of relatives in law enforcement. He complained about the cost of fueling his trucks.

"I'm not hardcore like I have to vote Republican," Delise told Reuters in a follow-up interview, adding that he had not ruled out backing a Democrat if he decides to vote. "I'd be open. I'm not saying there's not a chance."

To be sure, many people canvassers encountered were already in Rogers' camp, making the conversations less about persuasion than turnout. One Trump supporter in her 50s said she and two family members had already committed to Rogers, while a middle-aged man chatting in a neighbor's yard said he would back Rogers to thwart what he described as a socialist turn by Democrats.

Trump and his allies have sought to capitalize on recent primary victories by some left-leaning Democrats like El-Sayed to argue that the party is veering toward socialism and poses a threat to the country, a claim Democratic leaders dismiss as false and fearmongering. At the same time, Trump has called on his party to put him at the center of their election efforts to excite his base, despite his growing unpopularity.

A Republican couple in their 80s illustrated a potential weakness in the Trump-centric turnout strategy. While the wife said she would vote for Rogers, her husband said dissatisfaction with the president had left him unsure whether he could back the Republican Senate nominee. A canvasser sought to redirect the conversation to policy differences and away from Trump.

"People aren't super happy with the situation in the world right now," Tim Golding, senior adviser to AFP Action in Michigan, said in an interview. "But we try to pivot off that conversation and go back to the policies and the agenda that our candidates have, and not have a conversation about Trump as best we can."

El-Sayed has pushed back against the characterization that he is a radical socialist, calling himself a capitalist. Campaign spokesperson Cole Wozniak said they had built a motivated grassroots base with more than 21,000 volunteers.

The Rogers campaign did not respond to a request for comment.

ENTHUSIASM GAP

With Trump posting weak approval ratings and not on the ballot, Republicans must mobilize supporters who might otherwise skip the midterms, when turnout typically falls by more than 10 percentage points from presidential-election levels. That historic trend is raising the stakes for the Republicans' national door-knocking and other get-out-the-vote efforts this election.

Democrats appear more energized, with 42% of self-described Democrats saying they are "very enthusiastic" about voting, compared with 28% of Republican voters, according to the latest Reuters/Ipsos poll.

In Michigan, concerns about an enthusiasm gap recently spilled into public view when a Republican working with the Rogers campaign complained about a lack of energy among volunteers for door-knocking and other activities.

"The vibes on the ground are the worst I've seen in my life," Jackson Karki, a college student who had been helping the campaign organize several northern counties, posted to X last week. "No one wants to promote candidates, no one wants to knock doors, no one wants to do shit."

Other Republicans dispute that characterization. In Oakland County, one of Michigan's most important battlegrounds and home to more than 1 million registered voters, Republican Party Chair Vance Patrick said volunteer enthusiasm remains strong.

In an interview, he said Trump was set to visit the state twice before the election on November 3, which he predicted would further encourage volunteers and boost turnout. County party organizations like Patrick's have grown more important in Michigan as the state Republican Party's operations have weakened in recent years.

Patrick said the county's top targets include roughly 20,000 Jewish voters, a key constituency for Rogers given El-Sayed's opposition to military aid for Israel and his characterization of Israel's actions in Gaza as genocide. It is also chasing 38,000 so-called sleeping giants - infrequent voters who they believe would back Rogers if persuaded to cast a ballot.

MICHIGAN A CASE STUDY OF NATIONAL EFFORT

Including AFP and other outside groups, Rogers' campaign plans to knock on six million to eight million doors by Election Day, according to a person familiar with the matter, roughly double the 2024 total, when he lost the Senate race by 19,000 votes.

The effort reflects the scale of the Republican turnout strategy nationally, where campaigns and allied groups are investing heavily in door-knocking and other voter-targeting operations amid concerns about voter enthusiasm.

Republicans hold a $637 million cash lead nationally over Democrats across super PACs and party committees, dwarfing Democrats' edge in candidate fundraising and potentially helping fund a more expansive turnout operation, said Brendan Glavin, OpenSecrets' director of insights.

Yet Democrats say money alone will not decide the race. The Michigan Democratic Party says its active volunteer ranks have grown by 267% since the primary as the party has rallied behind El-Sayed.

Michigan Democratic Party Chair Curtis Hertel said Democrats will knock on 1.4 million doors in the campaign's final four weeks, arguing the effort will blunt Republican attempts to shift focus away from kitchen-table issues.

They are counting on voters like one resident in his 20s who answered the door in Livonia and, when asked whom he planned to vote for, replied simply, "Not Mike Rogers," before closing it.

data.title: PVR INOX opens five-screen multiplex in Kochi, expands network to 1,797 screens
data.description:
PVR INOX Limited has opened a new five-screen multiplex at MyMoon in Kochi, Kerala. In an exchange filing, the company said the new cinema is fitted with PXL, 4K laser projection, Dolby Atmos sound and RealD 3D technology across its five screens, which together seat 814 people. With the addition, PVR INOX said its network now stands at 1,797 screens across 358 properties in 114 cities in India and Sri Lanka.

The property, on Chittoor Road, draws on Kerala's art and design traditions, with handcrafted and vintage-style interior elements running through the space. It described the cinema as built around a "multiplex in a garden" concept, incorporating reclaimed wood and plants throughout the property, alongside antique film and music-related props in its common areas. The foyer includes a coffee kiosk and seating, and the property has a food street accessible from both ends, with ordering via what the company called "piano windows."

On the food and beverage side, PVR INOX said the property offers tiered pricing, including MRP-priced items, weekday deals, and separate vegetarian, health-focused and children's menus, along with self-service ordering kiosks. The release also said customers get unlimited refills with large popcorn and cola purchases. Four of the five auditoriums have premium recliners in the back row, while the fifth has lounger seating instead, and each auditorium has its own distinct design theme.

The shares of PVR Inox ended marginally higher in the session on Friday, September 25. The stock has jumped 23.7% in the year so far.

data.title: Gold Fields expresses interest in buying Northern Star, Bloomberg reports
data.description:
South African miner Gold Fields has expressed interest in buying Australia's largest gold miner Northern Star , Bloomberg News reported on Saturday, citing people with knowledge of the matter.

Here are further details:

  • Gold Fields recently approached Northern Star about a transaction, Bloomberg said.

  • However, the Australian miner rebuffed the overtures, and Gold Fields is considering its next steps, Bloomberg said.

  • Gold Fields and Northern Star did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment outside business hours.

data.title: The Vvaan box office: Sidharth Malhotra's latest beats opening day figures of his recent releases, earns Rs 8.12 cr
data.description:
New Delhi, Sept. 26 -- Sidharth Malhotra and Tamannaah Bhatia's 'The Vvaan: Force of the Forrest' has opened in theatres with a collection of Rs 8.12 crore on its first day.

The film had a decent start at the box office on Friday, September 25, amid mixed reviews. It also faced a theatrical clash with the re-release of 'Avengers: Endgame', which has reportedly attracted audiences in cinemas.

According to trade analyst Taran Adarsh, the folk horror fantasy thriller collected Rs 8.12 crore nett across India on its opening day.

With its opening day collection, 'The Vvaan' has also earned more than Sidharth Malhotra's last three theatrical releases, 'Param Sundari', 'Yodha' and 'Thank God'.

While 'Param Sundari' collected Rs 7.37 crore on its opening day, 'Yodha' earned Rs 4.25 crore. 'Thank God', which released on a Tuesday during Diwali, opened with Rs 8.10 crore, Taran Adarsh said.

The film's opening day collection has given it a start ahead of these three releases, with its weekend performance now likely to be closely watched.

'The Vvaan: Force of the Forrest' brings together TVF's Arunabh Kumar, director Deepak Mishra and Ektaa Kapoor. The film combines folklore, fantasy, adventure, mystery and humour.

The film stars Sidharth Malhotra and Tamannaah Bhatia in the lead roles. It is presented by Balaji Motion Pictures, a division of Balaji Telefilms Ltd, in association with TVF and 11.11 Production. Shobha Kapoor, Ektaa R Kapoor, Arunabh Kumar and Niraj Kothari have produced the film, while Manu Anand serves as its Director of Photography and Visual Director.

'The Vvaan: Force of the Forrest' was released in theatres on September 25.

data.title: Bangladesh launches measles vaccination drive amid deadly outbreak
data.description:
Bangladesh launched a nationwide measles-rubella vaccination campaign on Saturday, targeting 3.4 million unvaccinated and missed children, amid its worst-ever measles outbreak, which has killed more than 1,000 people and infected tens of thousands.

The month-long campaign aims to vaccinate children aged 6 months to 59 months who missed earlier immunisation efforts after authorities lowered the minimum vaccination age from the usual 9 months because of the outbreak.

The outbreak has exposed gaps in childhood immunisation and put growing pressure on health services, already grappling with a seasonal surge in dengue infections.

Bangladesh is currently experiencing the world's largest measles outbreak, according to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. It has recorded 1,087 confirmed and suspected measles-related deaths, including 101 laboratory-confirmed fatalities.

Since March 15, authorities have reported nearly 187,000 suspected cases and 21,099 confirmed infections, with more than 165,000 people hospitalised, health ministry data showed.

Health experts attributed the crisis to disruptions in routine immunisation programmes in 2024 and 2025, when political turmoil, changes to vaccine procurement and the postponement or cancellation of vaccination campaigns left many children unprotected.

Missed vaccinations and vaccine supply disruptions left children vulnerable to infection, particularly infants under 9 months who are too young to receive routine measles immunisation, helping fuel transmission across age groups.

Since April, Bangladesh has vaccinated nearly 20 million children through emergency and follow-up campaigns. However, experts say significant immunity gaps remain, with many eligible children still unvaccinated or missed during previous drives.

They say reaching every eligible child in the latest campaign will be critical to slowing transmission and preventing future outbreaks of the highly contagious disease.

Authorities said the campaign will help close immunity gaps, reduce severe illness and deaths, and break chains of transmission across Bangladesh.

data.title: Category 5 Hurricane Polo threatens Mexico’s coast, landfall expected Monday
data.description:
By Leila Miller

Hurricane Polo moved away from Mexico's Pacific coast on Saturday after it regained the highest Category 5 ​strength, before an expected return to make landfall in Baja California Sur on Monday, forecasters said.

On Saturday morning, Polo was about 425 miles south west of the Mexican resort town of Cabo Corrientes, with maximum sustained winds of 160 mph, according to the US National Hurricane Center. The storm was moving north west at 10 mph.

AccuWeather, a private ​forecaster, reported that 24 hours after hitting Baja California, the hurricane was expected to make a second landfall along the coast of mainland northwestern Mexico, bringing potential life-threatening flash flooding to parts of Baja California Sur, Sinaloa, Sonora and Chihuahua.

The hurricane’s heavy rain and strong winds along Mexico’s Pacific coast forced evacuations, port closures and school cancellations this week. ​In the resort city of San Jose del Cabo, police officers restricted access to a beach on Friday as the hurricane generated high waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Hurricane conditions are possible on Monday afternoon from Punta Eugenia to Santa Fe in Baja California, the NHC said.

Polo is expected to dump 4 to 8 inches of rain across parts of Baja California Sur, with maximum amounts of 10 inches, which could produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides, the NHC said. It could also cause life-threatening surf, rip currents and coastal flooding.

data.title: Tom Lee Says ‘Stay Tuned’ As Bitmine Nears 5% Ethereum Goal, Hints At What’s Next
data.description:
Key points:
  • Tom Lee said on Thursday that Bitmine reached its 5% ETH goal years ahead of schedule.
  • Lee hinted at a new long-term target but declined to disclose specifics.
  • The company says plans will balance Ethereum ecosystem support and shareholder value.

Bitmine Immersion Technologies (BMNR) Chairman Tom Lee said that the company was close to owning 5% of all Ethereum (ETH) and told investors to "stay tuned" for what comes next, stopping short of naming a new target.

Speaking on the Coinage podcast on Thursday, Lee explained that the 5% goal had arrived years ahead of schedule. He said that Bitmine had set that level because it was a quantity of ETH large enough "to have a positive influence on the Ethereum ecosystem," funded in part by staking yields.

The company had expected it to take five years, but he said that, "We're only 1.2 years into it, but I think we're pretty close to reaching that 5% target now," Lee said.

When Lee was asked whether the next goal of BMNR was owning 10% of Ethereum, he explained that the company had spent recent months "in consultation with the foundation, a lot of stakeholders in crypto, actually a lot of companies too, and some regulators." He said the objectives would not change, naming a beneficial impact on the Ethereum ecosystem and maximizing shareholder value.

Treasury Nears 5% Mark

This comes as Bitmine made a fresh ETH purchase over the past week. The firm held 5,983,940 ETH as of the day before, or about 4.9% of the 122.1 million ETH in supply. The company described that as 98% of the way to what it calls the "Alchemy of 5%," reached in 15 months. It said 5,067,309 ETH were staked, and put its combined crypto, cash, and marketable securities at just over $17 billion.

Lee also defended the company's returns against the token it held. He said Bitmine beat Ethereum by about 45 percentage points from June 30 to year-end last year, and by roughly 13 points this year. The stock now trades at close to the value of what it holds.

BMNR’s price closed down over 1% on Friday, with a market cap of about $16.6 billion. On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment around BMNR remained in the ‘neutral’ zone, while chatter around it shifted to ‘high’ from ‘normal’ over the past day.

Signals Of A Shift

Lee has hinted before that Bitmine's purchases go beyond Ethereum. He said in May that the company could slow its Ethereum purchases for "other things" in crypto, and it has previously funded share buybacks by easing off ETH accumulation.

Ethereum’s price was also down by 1% during the past 24 hours. On Stocktwits Ethereum was the top trending ticker. Retail sentiment around ETH remained in the ‘bullish’ zone, while chatter around it stayed at ‘normal’ levels over the past day.

BMNR stock has been up over 1% so far this year, down over 44% in the last 12 months. Meanwhile, ETH has been down over 9% so far this year, down over 33% in the last 12 months.

data.title: Grand Continent Hotels launches new hotel at Vellore
data.description:
Hospitality chain Grand Continent Hotels has announced the launch of its 32nd hotel - Grand Continent Premier Vellore.

The new 50-room hotel has been designed to cater to business travellers, medical tourists, students and their families, leisure travellers and pilgrimage groups visiting Vellore.

“With the launch of our 32nd property, we are further strengthening our presence in South India while continuing to expand into markets where we see sustained demand. Our focus remains on building a well-connected portfolio across business, healthcare, pilgrimage and leisure destinations, while maintaining consistency in service and guest experience,” Ramesh Siva, Founder & Managing Director, Grand Continent Hotels Limited, said.

With the addition of the Vellore property, Grand Continent Hotels has expanded its presence to 32 hotels across 20 cities with more than 2,000 keys.

The company’s portfolio includes destinations such as Bengaluru, Chennai, Hyderabad, Gurgaon, Hosur and Secunderabad.

data.title: SECL Plans $800 Mn IPO, Hires Top Banks
data.description:
SECL IPO 2026 could raise up to $800 million, with Coal India’s subsidiary appointing four banks for the proposed Mumbai listing

South Eastern Coalfields Ltd (SECL), one of Coal India Ltd’s largest subsidiaries, has appointed investment banks for a proposed Mumbai initial public offering that could raise up to USD 800 million, as the state-run miner advances plans to list its major subsidiaries.

SECL has appointed ICICI Securities, SBI Capital Markets, Motilal Oswal Investment Advisors and IDBI Capital Markets & Securities to advise on the proposed share sale, according to people familiar with the matter.

SECL could file its draft prospectus as early as December, although the size and timing of the offering remain under discussion and could change. Coal India is expected to sell part of its stake through an offer for sale (OFS), meaning the parent company would be the primary beneficiary of the share sale rather than SECL receiving the entire IPO proceeds.

SECL IPO Part Of Coal India Listing Plan

The proposed IPO is part of Coal India’s broader plan to unlock value from its subsidiaries. Coal India Chairman and Managing Director B Sairam said in August that the company planned to bring both SECL and Mahanadi Coalfields Ltd (MCL) to the market within FY27, with the exact timing dependent on market conditions and government directives.

MCL has already filed a draft prospectus with the Securities and Exchange Board of India, while Coal India plans to sell as many as 661.8 million shares in that offering. The proposed SECL listing would add another large state-owned coal producer to India’s primary-market pipeline.

The move follows two Coal India subsidiaries, Bharat Coking Coal Ltd and Central Mine Planning & Design Institute, making market debuts in FY26. The government, which holds more than 61 per cent of Coal India, remains the largest shareholder in the parent company.

SECL Among Coal India’s Largest Producers

SECL operates 60 coal mines across central India, including 35 mines in Chhattisgarh and 25 in Madhya Pradesh. It is a Mini Ratna subsidiary of Coal India and remains a major contributor to the parent company’s coal-production operations.

Coal India’s subsidiary-listing strategy comes amid sustained activity in India’s IPO market, with companies seeking to tap domestic institutional and retail capital. However, the SECL transaction remains at an early stage, and its final valuation, issue size, share-sale structure and listing timeline will depend on regulatory approvals, market conditions and government decisions.

data.title: Personality Rights in India: Voice Cloning, Image Misuse and the Case for IT Act Reform
data.description:
Indian law protects identity through privacy, publicity and intellectual property doctrines, but AI-driven misuse is exposing gaps that targeted IT Act reform could address says Rajeshwari Hariharan, Senior Advocate

Can an actor stop an advertiser from copying her voice? Can a teacher object when her photograph appears in an advertisement without permission? Does a much photographed animal have “personality rights”? These questions are often grouped under the singular label of “personality rights”, but they concern different legal interests. An identity can be commercially valuable. It can also be deeply personal even when its owner is unknown to the public.

Personality rights describe a person’s claim to control certain uses of the attributes by which others recognise them: a name, image, likeness, voice, signature or other distinctive feature. Within that broad description, publicity rights usually concern the commercial appropriation of identity. Privacy and dignity address a wider range of intrusions, including uses from which nobody profits. Indian law protects these interests through several doctrines rather than one comprehensive personality rights statute. Understanding the difference between them matters more than choosing a single label.

In India, personality rights are not set out as a single, self-contained statutory right. They draw on several areas of law: the constitutional right to privacy and dignity under Article 21; the common-law right of publicity against unauthorised commercial use of identity; and, where the facts permit, passing off, trade mark law, copyright in a particular photograph or recording, defamation and data protection law. These protections address different wrongs under different fact conditions. For example, copyright in a photograph is distinct from the depicted person’s claim against misuse of their identity.

Why does the law protect identity?

The clearest case is a false endorsement. If a business puts a well-known actor’s photograph on its advertisement, consumers may believe the actor has approved the product. The business obtains attention and credibility for which it has neither paid nor secured permission. The actor loses control over an endorsement that may have substantial commercial value.

In Titan Industries Ltd v Ramkumar Jewellers, [CS(OS) 2662/11 (order dtd 26.4.12) the Delhi High Court dealt with advertisements using images of Amitabh and Jaya Bachchan associated with a Tanishq campaign. In that case, Tanishq engaged Amitabh and Jaya Bachchan to endorse its widely advertised “True Diamonds” Diwali campaign. The plaintiff alleged that Ramkumar Jewellers copied its hoardings and used the Bachchans’ images to suggest they endorsed its jewellery, thereby infringing copyright and passing off its goods as associated with Tanishq. Since the defendant had never engaged the Bachchans, the Court injuncted the defendant from using the images of the Bachchans.

This was a very early case of misuse of personality rights.

Similarly, a fabricated recording (through AI) can also make someone appear to utter words they never said. An intimate AI image can be created around a person’s face without any authentic image of the supposed event. In such cases, the wrong includes the false attribution of conduct and the loss of control over one’s representation. Common law protects identity because it is connected both to economic opportunity and to personal autonomy.

This distinction also explains why a remedy must be tailored. A false advertisement may justify restraint, damages or an account of profits, depending on the claim and proof. An invasive image may require immediate removal and protection of privacy even if its creator earned nothing.

Personality rights and intellectual property

Personality rights frequently appear in intellectual property litigation, but a human being is not an item of intellectual property. The what is it? Copyright protects eligible works, such as a photograph, film or sound recording; it does not give the person depicted in a photograph copyright merely because their face appears in it. The photographer, producer, performer and depicted person may have different rights arising from the same material. Their contracts may allocate some of those rights, but a contract concerning a recording should not automatically be read as consent to every future imitation of the person’s identity.

Trademark law can protect a name or other sign when it functions as a mark and the statutory requirements are met. Passing off may address a misleading suggestion of commercial association. Neither doctrine provides a general monopoly over every mention of a name. Conversely, a person need not register their face or voice as a trade mark before objecting to a harmful, unauthorised use.Thankfully, common law rights are well recognized by courts.

The case law reflects this mixture of interests. In ICC Development (International) Ltd v Arvee Enterprises, 2003(26)PTC245(DEL) the Delhi High Court distinguished an individual’s right of publicity from a corporation’s asserted “persona” in a sporting event. The decision located publicity in the individual and the identifying attributes of that individual.

In D.M. Entertainment Pvt Ltd v Baby Gift House MANU/DE/2043/2010, the Court addressed the commercial exploitation of singer Daler Mehndi’s persona through merchandise and injuncted use of Mr. Mehndi's persona for the purpose of capitalizing upon his name by using it in conjunction with the commercial products since it gives rise to a false belief that, plaintiff has either licensed or the Defendants have some connection with them (i.e. the plaintiff or the artist), to use its exclusive right to market images of the artist.

Recent disputes have made these principles more pressing. In Anil Kapoor v Simply Life India [CS(COMM) 652/2023 and I.A. 18237/2023-18243/2023- order dtd 29.9.23], the Delhi High Court injuncted unauthorised use of the actor’s name, image, voice, catchphrases, including use involving AI and deepfakes by third parties without his consent

In Arijit Singh v Codible Ventures LLP [COM IPR SUIT (L) NO.23443 OF 2024 order dtd 26.7.24]  the Bombay High Court considered AI tools capable of imitating the singer’s voice and granted interim relief on the facts before it. These orders show how a familiar concern: the unauthorised use of a recognisable identity can arise through new means of reproduction. They remain fact-specific interim decisions, not declarations that every imitation requires a licence.

Does an ordinary person have a personality?

Yes. But fame may increase the commercial value of an identity; it does not create the identity or the person’s entitlement to dignity. An ordinary person has a name, voice, likeness and reputation. Their photograph cannot be put into a misleading endorsement merely because they lack celebrity status. A voice clone used to defraud their family may be more damaging to them than an unauthorised advertisement is to a performer.

There is nevertheless a practical difference between each of these kinds of claims. A celebrity alleging loss of an endorsement opportunity may be able to prove the market value of their persona. A person with no endorsement business may have little basis for that particular measure of damages. They may still establish deception, defamation, an invasion of privacy or another actionable injury. The remedy should follow the interest infringed, rather than assume that every plaintiff has a licensing market.

Indian judgments often discuss publicity rights in the light of celebrity cases because those disputes reach commercial courts. That history should not turn “celebrity” status into a condition for protecting an individual’s identity. An ordinary claimant’s rights would lie in privacy and dignity, especially where the use is intimate, humiliating or coercive.

Where privacy begins and publicity ends

Publicity and privacy overlap, but neither fully contains the other. Publicity ordinarily asks whether someone has appropriated the commercial value of an identifiable person. Privacy asks, among other things, whether a use intrudes upon the person’s autonomy or dignity. An unauthorised advertisement may engage both. A non-commercial intimate deepfake may engage privacy profoundly even when no endorsement is suggested.

The Supreme Court’s decision in Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) v Union of India, (2017) 10 SCC 1, supplies the constitutional foundation for privacy as an aspect of dignity and autonomy. Its reasoning supports protection against serious misrepresentation of a person’s identity, although it did not itself decide a personality rights dispute involving AI. Data protection may also regulate the processing of personal photographs or recordings, but its obligations and commencement must be examined provision by provision. It does not, on its own, resolve every question about a published depiction.

There is a corresponding freedom of expression. A biography necessarily names its subject. A cartoon may exaggerate a politician’s features. Sports coverage reports players’ names and performances. In Digital Collectibles Pte Ltd v Galactus Funware Technology[ CS(COMM) 108/2023 order dtd 26.4.23], the Delhi High Court emphasised free expression when considering the use of cricketers’ names, images and publicly available performance information in an online fantasy sports setting. The case cautions against turning publicity into control over every public reference to a person.

Courts therefore need to ask what the challenged use does. Does it falsely suggest endorsement? Does it take an identity to sell a product? Does it reveal or fabricate something intimate? Is the person identifiable? Was the use authorised? Would a reasonable audience understand the work as reporting, commentary or fiction? The answers should determine the cause of action and the scope of relief.

Is a new law needed?

Current law can resolve many clear cases. Copyright can protect a copied photograph or recording. Trade mark and passing off law can address misleading commercial association. Privacy, defamation and established civil remedies can respond to other injuries. The recent personality rights orders demonstrate that courts can grant urgent, focused relief without waiting for Parliament.

The present framework though sufficient is less clear at its edges. It does not offer one settled account of which attributes are protected, what conduct constitutes infringement, whether commercial gain is necessary, how consent to one use affects another, or what happens to a publicity claim after death. In Krishna Kishore Singh v Sarla A Saraogi,[ CS(CoMM) 187/2021-order dtd 11.7.23] concerning a proposed work about Sushant Singh Rajput, the Court categorically held that personality rights cease on the death of the person and the heirs cannot seek to injunct the telecast of a film on the ground of violation of SSR's personality rights – the case illustrates the difficulty of treating posthumous personality claims as self-evident under existing law. Any statute should confront that question expressly instead of leaving it to assumptions about inheritance.

Conclusion: Amend the Information Technology Act

India need not enact a separate personality rights law. The more useful step is to add a chapter on misuse of personal identity to the Information Technology Act, 2000. The Act already addresses electronic impersonation and provides a framework for intermediary duties, making it a practical home for remedies against digital misuse of a person’s name, image, likeness or voice.

The amendment should give every identifiable person, not only a celebrity, a civil remedy when their attributes are used without consent to falsely suggest endorsement, depict conduct that did not occur, or cause serious injury to privacy or reputation. It should make clear that consent to one use, such as an interview or advertisement, does not authorise a new AI-generated use. Courts should be empowered to order prompt, precisely identified takedown, preservation of evidence, injunctions and damages.

The provision must also preserve reporting, biography, criticism, parody and other expression that does not deceptively claim a person’s participation or endorsement.

Such an amendment would leave copyright to protect works and trade mark law to protect marks, while addressing the distinct harm caused by misusing a person’s identity through a complete code. Existing law supplies the foundation. A focused amendment would make its protection clearer and accessible to the common person whose identity may have no market price but is no less their own.

By Rajeshwari Hariharan, Senior Advocate

data.title: Gold May Reach USD 5,000/Oz In H1 2027 As Dollar, US Real Yields Ease: ICICI Bank
data.description:
Report Sees Strong Gold Demand From Central Banks And Investors Supporting Prices Despite Near-Term US Policy Pressures

Gold prices could rise to USD 4,600-USD 5,000 per ounce in the first half of 2027 as easing US real yields and a softer dollar provide support to bullion, ICICI Bank said in a research report. The bank expects prices to remain elevated through the remainder of 2026, with gold likely to trade in the USD 4,200-USD 4,600 per ounce range before gaining a marginal upside bias in H1 2027.

Gold has corrected sharply in September after gaining around 9 per cent in August, with prices down nearly 8 per cent during the month so far. ICICI Bank attributed the decline to a more hawkish repricing of US monetary policy, persistent inflation concerns, higher oil prices and stronger-than-expected labour market data.

Despite the recent correction, the bank said these near-term pressures may not be sufficient to reverse the broader strength in bullion. Investment demand, continued central bank purchases and gold's role as a hedge against geopolitical, financial and policy uncertainty are expected to support the medium-term outlook.

Gold ETFs recorded USD 17.8 billion of inflows in August, taking third-quarter gold ETF demand to 144.7 tonnes. The People's Bank of China bought 20 tonnes of gold during the month, marking its largest monthly purchase since October 2023.

ICICI Bank said concerns over the long-term sustainability of US fiscal deficits and high public debt could continue to support demand for gold. Central bank diversification away from US dollar-denominated assets and the metal's role as a portfolio hedge are also expected to remain structural supports.

The bank said easing global energy pressures could further strengthen the outlook for bullion. As energy pressures come off, it expects an increasing likelihood of gold trading with an upside bias.

India Demand Remains Constrained

For India, ICICI Bank expects domestic gold prices to remain largely driven by global bullion prices, while rupee movements could add another source of volatility. The bank retained its forecast for domestic gold prices at Rs 1.40 lakh-Rs 1.60 lakh per 10 grams through the remainder of 2026.

Domestic jewellery demand remains constrained by elevated gold prices, although wedding demand has remained relatively resilient. Festive and wedding activity is expected to provide some support to consumption, while India's gold imports fell to USD 2.3 billion in August from USD 4.2 billion in July.

At the same time, Indian gold ETF inflows rose to Rs 26 billion in August. The combination of weaker physical imports and stronger ETF inflows points to continued investment interest even as elevated prices weigh on jewellery demand.

data.title: SBI Hands Over Rs 500 Cr Cheque To Jeevika Didis In Bihar
data.description:
Funding will support women-led self-help groups and strengthen access to credit for livelihood and income-generating activities

State Bank of India (SBI) has handed over a cheque worth Rs 500 crore to Jeevika Didis in Patna to support women-led self-help groups and expand access to finance for livelihood activities.

The funding is aimed at strengthening financial support for women associated with Jeevika, Bihar’s rural livelihoods programme, and enabling self-help groups to undertake and expand income-generating activities.

Funding To Support Women-Led Groups

The Rs 500-crore support is expected to provide additional financial resources to women’s self-help groups operating across Bihar. The funds can help groups expand existing livelihood activities and invest in small businesses and other income-generating ventures.

The initiative comes as banks and the state government continue to expand formal credit access for women linked to Jeevika. The State Level Bankers’ Committee in Bihar has also reviewed bank linkages and individual financing for women associated with Jeevika-affiliated self-help groups.

Focus On Financial Inclusion

Jeevika has emerged as a major platform for connecting rural women with financial services, credit and livelihood opportunities through self-help groups.

The latest funding support is part of the broader push to strengthen institutional finance for women in rural areas. Increased access to bank credit can help self-help groups expand businesses, improve household incomes and create local employment opportunities.

The initiative also comes amid a wider focus on women-led economic activity in Bihar. A separate Community Investment Fund of around Rs 500 crore was recently announced for women, with the money to be channelled through cluster-level federations supporting self-help groups.

data.title: Suraj Estate subsidiary completes over ₹82 crore Mahim development rights acquisition
data.description:
Suraj Estate Developers said its wholly owned subsidiary Iconic Property Developers Private Limited has completed the acquisition of development rights for a 2,941-square-metre plot in Mahim (West), Mumbai.

The company said the development agreement for the plot, which is contiguous to its ongoing commercial project Suraj One Business Bay, has been registered and the acquisition has been completed with a total investment of ₹82.72 crore.

Following amalgamation with the existing commercial development, the plot is expected to add around 1.50 lakh square feet of saleable carpet area, with an estimated gross development value (GDV) of about ₹800 crore, according to the company's exchange filing dated September 25.

Suraj Estate said the acquisition is expected to strengthen its near-to-medium-term project pipeline and consolidate its presence in South-Central Mumbai.

The ₹800-crore GDV is an estimate disclosed by the company and represents the potential value of the additional development; it is not reported revenue or profit from the acquisition.

data.title: Prestige Estates issues corporate guarantee of up to ₹750 crore for subsidiary loan
data.description:
Prestige Estates Projects has issued a corporate guarantee of up to ₹750 crore to secure a loan being availed by its subsidiary, Prestige Falcon Mumbai Realty Private Ltd, the company said in a regulatory filing on September 25.

The guarantee has been provided in favour of ICICI Bank for the loan facility availed by the subsidiary.

According to the filing, the guarantee is being provided on an arm’s-length basis and in compliance with applicable provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 and SEBI listing regulations. The company said the promoter and promoter group do not have any interest in the transaction.

Prestige Estates said the corporate guarantee represents a contingent liability for the company. Since the guarantee has been provided on behalf of a subsidiary that forms part of the consolidated group, there is no immediate impact on the company, it said.

The disclosure was made under Regulation 30 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015.

Separately, Prestige Estates said its subsidiary Prestige Hospitality Ventures Ltd (PHVL) has withdrawn its Draft Red Herring Prospectus (DRHP) filed with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) for a proposed initial public offering (IPO) of its equity shares.

PHVL had filed the DRHP dated April 24, 2025 with SEBI, the National Stock Exchange of India and BSE, the company said in a separate exchange filing.

The board of directors of PHVL decided to withdraw the DRHP on September 25, 2026, citing strategic considerations and uncertain market conditions.

The withdrawal relates to the proposed IPO and is separate from the corporate guarantee disclosed by Prestige Estates for the Mumbai-based subsidiary.

data.title: Rs.8 interim dividend declared; check company, record date, payment date
data.description:
New Delhi, Sept. 26 -- R Systems International has announced a second interim dividend for financial year 2026, with shareholders now looking at the record date to determine their eligibility for the payout.

The company declared a second interim dividend of Rs.8 per equity share for 2026. The payout represents 800% of the equity share's face value of Re 1. The dividend is scheduled to be paid on or before October 24, 2026, according to the board meeting outcome.

The company informed the stock exchanges that its board approved the second interim dividend at its meeting held on September 25, 2026.

According to the company's exchange filing, the record date for determining shareholders' entitlement to the second interim dividend has been fixed for October 1, 2026. The disclosure was made pursuant to Regulation 42 of the Securities and Exchange Board of India's (SEBI) Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements Regulations, 2015.

The record date will determine which shareholders are entitled to receive the dividend.

The latest payout follows an earlier Rs.6 per share interim dividend declared by R Systems in March 2026. Including the latest Rs.8 payout, the company has announced Rs.14 per equity share in interim dividends for 2026 so far.

R Systems International ended 1% lower at Rs.235.70 per share on BSE on Friday, 25 September.

It had hit its 52-week high of Rs.446.55 in October 2025, while it touched its 52-week low of Rs.213.50 in July 2026. The stock has been under pressure in recent times, down 3% in 1 month, 6% in 3 months, 8% in 6 months and 45% in the last 1 year.

R Systems International posted a strong performance in the first quarter of 2026, with consolidated net profit climbing 69.5% year-on-year to Rs.65.41 crore. The growth came alongside a 29.9% increase in revenue from operations, which reached Rs.574.77 crore compared with Q1 2025.

Adjusted EBITDA rose 50.6% year-on-year to Rs.115.7 crore, or US$12.6 million. The company's EBITDA margin expanded to 20.1% in Q1 2026 from 17.4% in the corresponding quarter of the previous year, reflecting improved operating efficiency and leverage.

R Systems International Managing Director and CEO Nitesh Bansal said the company entered 2026 with continued momentum as mid-market enterprises increasingly shifted their focus from AI pilots towards full-scale, production-ready deployments.

He noted that the company's revenue growth of around 30% was supported by sustained demand for engineering services, along with the early contribution from EXIQO. The company's AI Studio combines AI-native talent, the OptimaAI platform and a governed delivery framework aimed at improving engineering velocity and generating measurable business outcomes.

Bansal added that the company began Q2 2026 with strong deal momentum and an expanding customer base, while its focus remained on helping clients convert their AI initiatives into sustained business value.

Meanwhile, R Systems CFO Nand Sardana said the company generated revenue of Rs.574 crore during Q1 2026 while maintaining an EBITDA margin of around 20%. He attributed the improvement to greater efficiencies and operating leverage from the company's platform-led business model.

Sardana also said R Systems continued to make disciplined investments in artificial intelligence during the quarter. The full-quarter consolidation of Novigo further contributed to strengthening the company's revenue and margin profile.

R Systems International is a digital product engineering company focused on designing and developing next-generation products, platforms and digital experiences. It works with clients across multiple industries, helping them pursue revenue growth and improve operational efficiency.

data.title: Blast in Pakistan's Dera Ismail Khan kills 11, injures 30
data.description:
Eleven people were killed and 30 injured in a blast in Dera Ismail Khan in northwestern Pakistan on Saturday, emergency service Rescue 1122 said.

Dera Ismail Khan, in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province near Pakistan's border regions with Afghanistan, has repeatedly been hit by Islamist militant violence, frequently targeting police and security forces.

The Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan claimed responsibility for Saturday's attack.

The blast occurred near Aman Mela in the Darazinda area of the district, Rescue 1122 said in a statement.

Rescue teams from the Darazinda station reached the scene and began relief operations, providing medical assistance to the wounded and taking them to hospital, the service said.

Security incidents have continued in the district this month, including attacks involving the Pakistani Taliban.

data.title: Fed requests comment on two proposals for stablecoin issuers under GENIUS Act
data.description:
The US Federal Reserve Board has requested public comment on two proposals for establishing a regulatory framework for supervised payment stablecoin issuers under the GENIUS Act.

The first would require issuers to fully back their stablecoins with reserve assets, including short-term Treasury bills and other high-quality, liquid assets, according to a release issued by the Fed on Thursday. It would also standardize capital requirements to address credit and operational risks and set risk-management standards.

The second proposal would establish an application process for banks seeking to issue payment stablecoins, requiring them to submit business plans and financial information. The proposal would also create a process for appeals, hearings and final determinations for applications.

The comment period will close 60 days after publication in the Federal Register.

Cointelegraph reported in July that US regulatory agencies had missed a rule-making deadline under the GENIUS Act, a year after the law was signed.

While several regulatory agencies published proposed rules and collected public feedback during the prededing year, no final regulations were issued before the deadline.

The GENIUS Act established the first comprehensive federal regulatory framework for stablecoins in the US. The act was signed into law by President Donald Trump on July 18, 2025.

data.title: Prestige Estates Withdraws Rs 2,700 Cr Hotel IPO Amid Market Uncertainty
data.description:
The planned issue was aimed at raising up to Rs 2,700 crore through a fresh public offering of PHVL’s equity shares

Prestige Estates Projects has withdrawn plans to take its hotel business public, withdrawing the draft offer document for a proposed Rs 2,700 crore initial public offering (IPO) amid uncertain market conditions and strategic considerations.

The Bengaluru-based real estate developer’s subsidiary, Prestige Hospitality Ventures (PHVL), had filed a draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) in April 2025 for the proposed IPO.

The planned issue was aimed at raising up to Rs 2,700 crore through a fresh public offering of PHVL’s equity shares. However, in a regulatory filing on 25 September, Prestige Estates said its board had decided to withdraw the DRHP.

The company attributed the decision to “strategic considerations and uncertain market conditions”, without providing further details on the factors behind the withdrawal.

Prestige Estates, however, has not ruled out a public listing of its hospitality business. PHVL may file a fresh DRHP with Sebi in the future, subject to suitable market conditions, the necessary regulatory approvals and other considerations, the company said.

The withdrawal comes as companies across sectors continue to assess IPO plans against prevailing market valuations and investor appetite. For Prestige Estates, the decision allows its hospitality business to defer the listing process while retaining the option of accessing public markets at a more suitable time.

PHVL houses Prestige Estates’ hospitality business, and a separate listing would have provided investors with direct exposure to the group’s hotel operations.

The proposed IPO had been part of Prestige Estates’ broader strategy to unlock value from its businesses through the capital markets. The company can now revisit the plan depending on market conditions and its strategic priorities.

data.title: Baanganga Gold & Diamond Files DRHP For Rs 720 Cr IPO
data.description:
Baanganga Gold & Diamond, an organised, fully integrated manufacturer of gold and diamond jewellery operating on a B2B model, has filed its Draft Red Herring Prospectus (DRHP) with Sebi for its proposed Initial Public Offering (IPO).

The offer comprises a fresh issue of equity shares aggregating up to Rs 540 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of up to Rs 180 crore, taking the total offer size to up to Rs 720 crore.

The OFS comprises shares offered by Promoter Selling Shareholders Navratanmal Jeetmal Ganna (up to Rs 120 crore) and Jinesh Navratanmal Ganna (up to Rs 60 crore).

The Company proposes to utilise the net proceeds from the fresh issue towards funding its working capital requirements and general corporate purposes. Of the proceeds, Rs 405 crore is proposed to be deployed towards funding working capital requirements, to be utilised across Fiscal 2027, Fiscal 2028 and Fiscal 2029.

Baanganga is engaged across the manufacturing value chain — product design, production, quality control and sale of gold and diamond jewellery — supplying primarily to organized corporate jewellery retail chains, wholesalers and distributors, including Joyalukkas India, Novel Jewels (Aditya Birla Group), Malabar Gold and Diamonds, Kalyan Jewellers, Bhima Enterprises and P N Gadgil Jewellers.

According to the CareEdge Report, the Indian wholesale gold jewellery market reached a value of Rs 2,176.1 billion in CY25, having grown at a CAGR of 11.3 per cent between CY20 and CY25, and is projected to reach Rs 4,024.7 billion by CY30P.

The organised segment's share of the historically fragmented industry has risen to around 35-40 per cent, led by pan-India players and regional brands. Baanganga holds a market share of approximately 1.9 per cent in the Indian gold jewellery manufacturing (wholesale) market in Fiscal 2026.

DAM Capital Advisors  is the sole book running lead manager to the offer. KFin Technologies is the registrar to the offer.
